findings.title: google.com fingerprinted your device (WebGL (GPU model))
findings.detail: Scripts from google.com (https://www.google.com/js/th/n_BHgtbTP3l_ff810bu_K6lL5wb_ZK3aoRJMIVk8Tks.js) used WebGL (GPU model) fingerprinting after you rejected cookies.
findings.law: PECR reg. 6 (consent needed to access information on a device, not just cookies); ICO guidance on fingerprinting
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 on consent; EDPB Cookie Banner Taskforce report (2023)

findings.title: Fingerprinting after rejection is not clearly explained in the cookie policy
findings.detail: After the cookie banner's optional cookies were rejected, scripts from google.com used WebGL to fingerprint the device. The cookie policy describes cookies and related technologies but does not clearly explain WebGL fingerprinting or how rejection prevents it.
findings.law: PECR reg. 6; UK GDPR Art. 5(1)(a) and Art. 13(1)
findings.policy_quote: When you visit our websites, data is automatically collected by the technology platforms providing the experience.
findings.reasoning: WebGL fingerprinting may involve reading device information and may require prior consent unless a narrow exception applies. The evidence does not establish advertising, profiling or the precise technical purpose, so medium is appropriate rather than high; however, the policy's general wording does not give clear information about this post-rejection activity.
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EU GDPR Art. 5(1)(a) and Art. 13(1)

ai_review.summary: The audit found WebGL device fingerprinting by google.com after the user rejected optional cookies. This raises a potential PECR consent issue and a clearer transparency concern, but the available evidence does not establish that the fingerprinting was used for advertising, profiling or session replay. The supplied privacy notice covers many UK GDPR topics, although it is specifically framed as a Shell Recharge notice.
evidence: E1: Cookie banner found: True. Reject clicked successfully: True. Method: selector. Buttons clicked: Reject optional cookies.
E2: Fingerprinting by scripts from google.com: webgl; phases: after_reject.
E3: Pages browsed and scrolled after reject: https://www.shell.co.uk/business.html, https://www.shell.co.uk/shell-go-plus.html, https://www.shell.co.uk/shell-service-stations.html.
E4: Privacy policy: https://www.shell.co.uk/privacy/shell-recharge.html. Companies it names: Shell Plc. Contact email found: privacy-eu@shellrecharge.com.

E6: Automated check (medium): google.com fingerprinted your device (WebGL (GPU model)). Scripts from google.com (https://www.google.com/js/th/n_BHgtbTP3l_ff810bu_K6lL5wb_ZK3aoRJMIVk8Tks.js) used WebGL (GPU model) fingerprinting after you rejected cookies.
